title: Personal LLM inference mini-tracker — Jamie (Q1 2026)
content:
Quick personal tracker for small inference experiments I run while iterating on runtime knobs and quantization profiles. Mostly a scratchpad — measurements are rough (local dev rig + small cloud instances), capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec and notes. Use as a quick reference before moving promising configs to the shared benchmark suite.

Table (columns: id | date | model | precision | batch | max_seq | p50_ms | p95_ms | tps | notes | next_steps | status)
1 | 2026-01-21 | gpt-neox-20b | fp16 | 1 | 512 | 72 | 145 | 38 | baseline on dev box (A100sm) | repro on Dedicated | done
2 | 2026-01-25 | gpt-neox-20b | int8 (GPTQ) | 1 | 512 | 85 | 200 | 52 | +best perf on tps but higher p95, KV cache warmup spike | try batching=2, profile kernel selection | in_progress
3 | 2026-02-03 | mixtral-8x7b | fp16 | 2 | 256 | 48 | 90 | 120 | good latency, scaling to batch=4 drops p50 slightly | test quant profile A | done
4 | 2026-02-10 | mixtral-8x7b | int4 (ptq) | 2 | 256 | 55 | 125 | 170 | promising tokens/sec, observed occasional output stuttering on long prompts | reproduce with long-context evals; run eval set | in_progress
5 | 2026-02-18 | vicuna-13b | fp16 | 1 | 1024 | 110 | 280 | 30 | high p95 for long seqs, CPU-side preproc causing stalls | move preproc to GPU pipeline, enable async io | todo
6 | 2026-02-23 | vicuna-13b | q4_0 | 1 | 1024 | 95 | 210 | 45 | quant reduces p50 but output quality check needed | run small evals (ROUGE, semantic) and human spot-checks | in_progress

Notes and heuristics:
- Always capture both p50 and p95; p95 reveals tail behavior from KV warmups and kernel fallbacks.
- TPS measured as tokens/sec during steady-state generation (exclude first 20 tokens to avoid warmup).
- For int8/4 runs note which quant tool/version (e.g., GPTQ v0.1.3, PTQ-v2); file an artifact if results look reproducible.
- Kernel fallback logs: look for messages about aten->fallback or memcpy stalls; correlate with p95 spikes.
- When testing batching changes, measure both latency/throughput and memory footprint (OOM risk for large seqs).

Short experiment checklist (my personal flow):
- Reproduce baseline on local dev (A100sm) -> capture p50/p95/TPS -> commit minimal repro script.
- Try quantized variant (same seed/prompt set) -> run 5 seeds (or 3) and compare output quality metrics.
- If throughput improves with acceptable quality, push to shared bench (link INF-3421) and add to model catalog notes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a quick cell to compute cost-per-1k-tokens using our internal price table (need updated per-GPU cost from finance).
- Create small automated eval harness for long-context stutter detection (needs signal + synthetic prompts).
- Talk to runtime team about kerning selection logs visibility in Dedicated (Maya assigned).

Quick links (local):
- small repro directory: ~/projects/inference-scratch/repros/jamie/q1-2026/
- logs: ~/projects/inference-scratch/logs/q1-2026/

Random notes to self:
- int4 PTQ looked good on mixtral but watch for hallucination increase in open-chat prompts.
- Batching=2 seemed to smooth p95 on int8 neox runs (might be reducing kernel churn).
- Remember to include seed+prompt-set in any shareable artifact.

If moving any row to the shared benchmark suite, add a small README describing exact machine (GPU model, CUDA/CUDNN/driver), container hash, quant tool + commit and the prompt set name.

End of mini-tracker.
summary: Personal mini-tracker for LLM inference experiments (latency, throughput, quantization tests). Scratchpad-style notes and next steps.
